thread:
maria: Heads-up — after the kernel + OFED roll in euc2 last night, we've seen ~30-50% throughput drop on NCCL all-reduce for large-model training. Jobs are intermittently falling back to TCP which doubles+ step time.
kevin: Seeing the same across p4 and p3 pools. NCCL logs show repeated 'unreachable' and then 'NET/TRANSPORT/TCP' messages before the job continues.
ajay: Can someone paste iperf/ib_write_lat from a failing host so we have numbers?
maria: Pasting quick metrics from gpu-111 -> gpu-112 (same rack):
```bash
# iperf3 -c gpu-112 -P 8
[SUM]  0.00-10.00  sec  18.3 GBytes  15.7 Gbits/sec
```
ib_write_lat snapshot: 
```
# baseline (pre-roll): ~0.7 us
# current: ~2.8 us (consistent across multiple runs)
```
lucy: That's ~4x latency increase. Also seeing mlx5/XRC errors in dmesg on several nodes: 
```
mlx5_core 0000:06:00.0: XRC: channel create failed -12
mlx5_core: Health: FW reported error STATUS_DUMP
```
diego: Found firmware divergence on a subset — gpu-111 shows FW 16.25.102, while gpu-112 is 16.30.110. The OFED playbook tried to upgrade but a few hosts skipped due to a reboot race.
infra-oncall-bot: Deploy event: kernel 5.4->5.15 + MLX_OFED 5.4 applied to euc2 at 03:12 UTC. Canary group was 10%. Rollout paused at 04:20 UTC after alerts.
kevin: My hunch: the newer OFED+kernel toggled a different mlx5 path (XRC/devx defaults) and some firmware versions respond poorly, leading to qp/channel creation failures and NCCL falling back. This matches a note in the vendor changelog.
ajay: Short-term mitigation: setting NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 in the training environment forces TCP and avoids the fallback churn. Not ideal (higher latency/cost) but stabilizes jobs.
lucy: Another quick test: toggling devx on mlx5 to see if it restores IPC performance. Can we try on a single canary host?
maria: Testing devx toggle now on gpu-113 (canary). Commands and result: 
```bash
# disable devx on host (requires root)
echo 0 > /sys/module/mlx5_core/parameters/enable_devx
# re-run ib_write_lat --> observed ~0.8 us again (near baseline)
```
diego: If disabling devx restores latencies, we can push a temporary cluster patch (sysctl/sysfs write via config management) while vendor/firmware alignment is scheduled.
kevin: Agreed. Plan of record and owners: 
- maria: continue canary monitoring + collect NCCL, dmesg, ibv_devinfo, ethtool stats from affected hosts (ETA 1h) :eyes:
- diego: inventory firmware/driver versions across euc2 and produce remediation list (rollback or forced fw update) (ETA 2h)
- ajay: draft emergency runbook to set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 for affected ML namespaces and notify ML-platform + ML teams (ETA 30m)
- lucy: open a support case with the NIC vendor (attach dmesg, ib stats, and OFED/kernel matrix) and request priority engineering review (now)
maria: Also flagging ML-platform to throttle heavy allreduce job submissions while we mitigate — @ml-platform please apply a temporary queue cap. :warning:
ajay: We'll also gate any further OFED/kernel rollout until vendor confirms compatibility and we have a clean canary pass in euc2. No cross-region rollouts for now.
infra-oncall-bot: Incident ticket INC-2026-045 created (priority P2), linked to deploy event 2026-03-18T03:12Z.
kevin: Thanks all. If canary remains green after devx toggle and sysfs patch, we can roll the mitigation to remaining hosts and start scheduled firmware normalization. :thumbsup:
maria: Will post updates in this thread. If you find noisy errors or newly failing jobs, ping me directly.
